kept.q: A bag contains 5 red balls, 3 blue balls, and 2 green balls, all of the same size and shape. A ball is picked at random from the bag. Find the probability that the ball picked is blue.
kept.explanation: Total balls = 5 + 3 + 2 = 10. Blue balls = 3. So P(blue) = 3/10.
kept.pidgin: Total balls na 5 + 3 + 2 = 10. Blue balls na 3. So P(blue) = 3/10.

kept.q: A fair six-sided die is thrown once. Find the probability of obtaining a number greater than 4.
kept.explanation: Numbers greater than 4 on a die are 5 and 6, that is 2 outcomes out of 6. So P = 2/6 = 1/3.
kept.pidgin: Numbers wey pass 4 for die na 5 and 6, na 2 outcomes out of 6. So P = 2/6 = 1/3.

kept.q: A basket contains 6 oranges and 4 mangoes. A fruit is picked at random and eaten, then a second fruit is picked from those remaining. Find the probability that both fruits picked are mangoes.
kept.explanation: P(first mango) = 4/10. After removing one mango, 3 mangoes remain out of 9 fruits, so P(second mango) = 3/9. Multiply: (4/10) x (3/9) = 12/90 = 2/15.
kept.pidgin: P(first mango) = 4/10. Wen we don remove one mango, 3 mango remain out of 9 fruits, so P(second mango) = 3/9. Multiply am: (4/10) x (3/9) = 12/90 = 2/15.

kept.q: The probability that Chidinma will pass Mathematics is 3/5, and the probability that she will pass English Language is 2/3. If the two events are independent, find the probability that she passes both subjects.
kept.explanation: For independent events, multiply the probabilities: P(both) = 3/5 x 2/3 = 6/15 = 2/5.
kept.pidgin: For independent events, multiply the probabilities: P(both) = 3/5 x 2/3 = 6/15 = 2/5.

kept.q: Two fair dice are thrown together once. Find the probability that the sum of the numbers that show up is 7.
kept.explanation: There are 36 equally likely outcomes when two dice are thrown. The pairs giving a sum of 7 are (1,6),(2,5),(3,4),(4,3),(5,2),(6,1), which is 6 outcomes. So P = 6/36 = 1/6.
kept.pidgin: 36 outcomes dey wen you throw two dice together. Pairs wey go give sum of 7 na (1,6),(2,5),(3,4),(4,3),(5,2),(6,1), wey be 6 outcomes. So P = 6/36 = 1/6.

kept.q: A class has 8 boys and 7 girls. Two students are selected at random from the class to represent it at a quiz competition. Find the probability that both students selected are girls.
kept.explanation: Total ways to choose 2 students from 15 is C(15,2) = 105. Ways to choose 2 girls from 7 is C(7,2) = 21. So P = 21/105 = 1/5.
kept.pidgin: Total ways to pick 2 students from 15 na C(15,2) = 105. Ways to pick 2 girls from 7 na C(7,2) = 21. So P = 21/105 = 1/5.
